description: The bar chart, titled “How Knowledge Popularity Influences and Enhances LLM Knowledge Boundary Perception,” illustrates the relationship between knowledge popularity and model performance across three domains — Movies, Songs, and Basketball — for three large language models: Llama3 (blue), Qwen2 (red), and ChatGPT (yellow). The vertical axis, labeled “Popularity,” ranges from 0 to 220 in increments of 20, indicating the popularity score of the knowledge domain. The horizontal axis categorizes the domains into three groups: Movies, Songs, and Basketball. Within each domain, performance is broken down into five subcategories, represented by distinct bar patterns: solid (Acc=0 & GT Ans), diagonal stripes (Acc=0 & Gene Ans), crosshatch (Acc=1 & GT Ans), and two others (Acc=0 & GT Ans and Acc=0 & Gene Ans) — though the legend appears to have a labeling inconsistency, as “Acc=0 & GT Ans” is listed twice with different patterns. In the Movies category, all models show low popularity scores, with Llama3 at approximately 30, Qwen2 at 40, and ChatGPT at 35. In Songs, popularity increases: Llama3 reaches ~70, Qwen2 ~85, and ChatGPT ~75. Basketball shows the highest popularity across all models: Llama3 peaks at ~180, Qwen2 at ~200, and ChatGPT at ~170. The chart visually emphasizes that as popularity increases (from Movies to Basketball), model performance (as measured by the popularity metric) also increases, with Qwen2 consistently achieving the highest scores in each domain. The bars are grouped by model within each domain, allowing for direct comparison of model performance across popularity levels.
